name: Hamilton Smith Hall
use: College of Liberal Arts classrooms and departments (English, Philosophy, and others)
architect: George Oakley Totten Jr. (original, 1905 blueprint); Eric T. Huddleston (1930s exterior); Koehler & Isaak (1959); DiMella Shaffer (2015–17)
style: Classical Revival library front with large columns; Colonial Revival reworking; contemporary rear addition

renovations.what: Exterior reworked in Colonial Revival style by Eric T. Huddleston (Clio dates this to 1937)
Converted from library to classrooms and offices after Dimond opened (Koehler & Isaak; Harvey Construction)
Rear addition (1965–66) for English, philosophy, history, government and sociology
Renovation and expansion: two-story central atrium rebuilt, 1965 addition replaced by a T-shaped wing, footbridge over the ravine, two WPA-era murals restored

facts.text: Built as the college library and Durham Public Library (1907–1958), funded by a $10,000 bequest from mining engineer Hamilton B. Smith plus a Carnegie grant.
The 2015–17 project cost $37 million and reconstructed a soaring two-story central atrium and airy front-wing classrooms; it reopened for Homecoming 2017 with a grand reopening on Sept. 22.
A new footbridge over the ravine links the building to the T-Hall parking lot, making the hall a main pedestrian route.
Two WPA-era murals completed in July 1940, when the building was the library, were restored; one had been hidden for decades, and the work was funded largely by Peter T. Paul '67.
Clio credits the surviving murals to George Lloyd (farming) and Arthur Esner (industry), and says recurring basement floods helped prompt the renovation.

verdict: The 1907 columned library turned liberal-arts hall, rebuilt in 2017 around a two-storey atrium with restored WPA murals.
notes: Original UNH Today URLs now redirect to the UNH Today home page, so Wayback snapshots are cited. Search snippets show Skanska listing the project as $30M / 95,000 sf, against UNH's $37M / 91,000 sf; the Skanska page now redirects and was not opened. Ceilings/light are from UNH's own description ('soaring two-story atrium', 'airy classrooms'); no licensed interior photo was found. No licensed modern exterior of the main facade was found on Commons or Flickr CC; the gallery has the 2018 bridge and historic library images. Reference photo ref-01 is the archives' pre-2015 view. Architect spelling: Clio writes 'DiMelia Shaffer'; the firm is DiMella Shaffer. No independent student reviews found.
judgeNotes: Exterior judged from historic postcards and the archives photo of the classical front; interior from published specs only, so confidence is capped at med. Reputation trimmed to 7: no student reviews were found. The footbridge shot moves behind the postcards because it barely shows the building.
